title: Delivery Claims Timing: Reporting Window, Delivered-Scan Wait and Lost-Parcel Threshold
content:
Three timing gates decide whether a Delivery Claims claim can be opened today. Each is read from the order's own dates in the records, never from the date the customer recalls.

## 1. Reporting window

A claim is opened only if it is reported no later than the claim type's reporting window, in calendar days, after the order is delivered — or, for a Lost in Transit Claim, after the order is dispatched (its shipped date).

- The anchor is the order's delivered date (shipped date for a Lost in Transit Claim) as recorded on the order.
- Window days are counted as calendar days after the anchor date, the anchor date being day zero, and the last day still qualifies.
- The claim may be opened on any day up to and including the last day of the window; from the following day it may not.

| Anchor date (hypothetical) | Window | Last day the claim may be opened | First day it may not |
|---|---|---|---|
| delivered 2 June | 30 calendar days | 2 July | 3 July |
| delivered 10 June | 7 calendar days | 17 June | 18 June |
| delivered 10 June | 14 calendar days | 24 June | 25 June |
| shipped on day zero | 60 calendar days | day 60 | day 61 |

## 2. Wait after the delivered scan

A Delivered Not Received Claim is opened only once the claim type's waiting period, in calendar days, has passed since the order is delivered, since carriers often scan before the parcel arrives.

- The clock starts on the order's delivered date, which is day zero; the day on which the waiting period is reached already qualifies.
- With the Delivered Not Received Claim's wait of 2 calendar days: an order delivered on 10 June (hypothetical) can carry a Delivered Not Received Claim from 12 June; on 10 June or 11 June it cannot.

## 3. Lost-parcel threshold

A Lost in Transit Claim is opened only once the parcel has shown no carrier movement for the claim type's ground threshold in business days on Economy Ground, Pickup Point Delivery or Standard Ground, or for its express threshold on faster services.

- Business days are Monday to Friday, excluding US federal holidays, counted from the last carrier scan of the parcel to today without a new scan.
- *Hypothetical:* a Standard Ground parcel at exactly 5 business days without movement has reached the 5-day threshold and may be claimed lost; at 4 business days it may not. A Next Business Day parcel at exactly 2 business days without movement may be claimed lost; at 1 business day it may not.

## The three gates together

| Gate | Applies to | Records read | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reporting window | every claim type | delivered date, or shipped date for Lost in Transit | no later than the last day |
| Delivered-scan wait | Delivered Not Received Claim | delivered date | no earlier than the day the wait is reached |
| Lost threshold | Lost in Transit Claim | carrier scans of the parcel | at least the threshold |
